dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Revenue Assurance analyst runs a read-only join of the 17 cluster `recharge_id`s to the entitlement store and the DLR-104/DLR-219 May settlement file"
"In parallel, add a non-blocking `posted_at − effective_event_date > 7` flag to the trend pack and restate the May West view on an effective-date basis."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Zero duplicates exist anywhere in the file" is somewhat broader than the tested duplicate definitions; internal identifier and near-duplicate checks cannot fully exclude economically duplicated events under different identifiers.
"No batch reprocessed or retried" is not fully established merely by observing that all batches were single-status RECONCILED; retry history or pipeline audit logs would provide stronger support.

"not manipulated reporting" is a strong conclusion from internal data and should remain conditional on the proposed entitlement and independent settlement checks, although the submission does identify those conditions explicitly.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative is a real duplicate or unfulfilled renewal masked by internally consistent pipeline records—for example, the same economic event loaded again under a different source_event_id, or amounts accepted by the pipeline without corresponding entitlement or external settlement. The analyst handled this well by preserving it as a material unknown and specifying entitlement, settlement, and source-extract checks.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute and report the independent entitlement and settlement reconciliation, including a reproducible test for economic duplicates under alternate identifiers; this would convert the principal remaining unknowns into verified controls.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "DiD -43.9pp (~-140 tickets)" is explicitly tied to tickets.csv `created_at`,`region` and matched pre/post windows.
"Only 6 of 1,098 dead-end sessions (0.5%) are followed by a South ticket ≤72h" identifies the IVR and ticket linkage and gives the cohort definition and result.

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Transfers 49.5%→3.3%; dead ends (ABANDONED+ERROR) 24.4%→40.5%" and the authentication error breakdown provide a concrete measurement-failure mechanism.

"Pilot suppressed ticket logging while demand and incidents rose" is supported by the exclusion described in the email, IVR failure stages, repeat contacts, and ticket linkage rather than ticket counts alone.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Material unknowns" explicitly states that "sentiment is unmeasured," case-creation history is unavailable, and callers who did not redial are invisible.

The submission tests seasonality, billing, data truncation, and low-value IVR chatter, including the alternative that "if a creation rule changed on 2026-05-10 the -38.4% is an artifact; if not" other evidence still argues against expansion.

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally" and "Hold at current scope" appropriately pause an underdetermined national inference rather than shutting down the pilot outright.
The proposed "shadow-log every dead-end session as a provisional case" and four-week remeasurement are reversible safeguards targeted at the suspected capture failure.

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: The note prioritizes a clear decision: "Freeze the pilot at South scope for 4 weeks" and specifies metrics, denominators, and a re-run point.
The five questions to Farah are operationally specific, including case-creation conditions, pre-auth reporting, outcome assignment, repeat contacts, and event messaging.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Ground truth moves opposite to tickets" overstates what service events and affected-account estimates establish; they are useful friction proxies, not direct ground truth about complaints or customer experience.

"the only two mechanisms that could make -38.4% real rather than an artifact" is too absolute. Other possibilities include genuine channel or process changes, selective population effects, or data/measurement changes outside the stated case-creation configuration.

"Only 6 of 1,098 dead-end sessions ... leave no CareDesk trace" conflates absence of a linked ticket with absence of a complaint; the analysis correctly notes this limitation elsewhere, but the wording is stronger than the evidence.
"Self-service cannot remove agent- and dealer-logged cases" is not fully established; NovaIVR could influence later contacts or routing even if those channels do not directly pass through the IVR.

"P1 share unchanged (6.6%→8.2%)" is imprecise: the displayed percentages differ materially, even if the change may not be statistically assessed. The phrase "all six issue types fell 29–50%" also needs the underlying category counts or query.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative is a real reduction in some logged demand combined with an independent CareDesk logging or routing change, rather than pure IVR suppression. The analyst partially handles this by stating that case-creation history is unknown and by noting that abandonment is not itself a complaint, but does not quantify or directly test genuine CX improvement among successful sessions.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Link IVR sessions, repeat contacts, service-event exposure, and all downstream case/contact outcomes at the subscriber or journey level, while listening to a stratified sample of successful, abandoned, and error sessions. This would distinguish genuine resolution from read-only lookup, abandonment without complaint, and unlogged complaints before any expansion decision.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks event wording against severity, zero impact_mw, duration_min, and cleared fields rather than treating alarming text as proof of failure.
It proposes the plausible innocent explanation that the extract may be filtered or limited to a particular date window.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It gives claim-specific confidence levels, including high confidence in timestamp ambiguity and low confidence that the ambiguity is currently causing an error.
It explicitly states that no rate, frequency, reliability, intent, or commercial-impact conclusion should be inferred.
The 90% confidence that the data are implausibly sparse is less well supported because max inverter_id does not necessarily establish a 22-unit fleet.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommended action—obtain the query filter and date range—is cheap, directly decision-changing, and proportionate.
The submission appropriately recommends stopping rather than escalating if provenance cannot be obtained.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly avoids inventing a plant problem from transient, cleared events with impact_mw equal to zero.
It is directionally correct that the extract cannot support frequency or reliability analysis without coverage provenance.
The conclusion somewhat overstates the file as an unusable export and the implication that INV-22 establishes a fleet of at least 22.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The highest ID present, INV-22, implies a fleet of at least 22 inverters" is not established unless inverter IDs are known to be contiguous fleet identifiers.
"Four events across 22+ units in nine days is implausibly sparse" depends on an unverified fleet denominator and on the extract being complete.

"Every structured field contradicts escalation" is too strong: zero MW impact, short duration, and cleared status contradict material operational impact, but they do not rule out a transient equipment or sensor issue.
"This is not a usable export" should be scoped to rate, frequency, and reliability analysis rather than all possible uses of the rows.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent six-day gap and low event count may be an artifact of a severity threshold, cleared-only selection, single reporting window, or other query filter; alternatively, the inverter IDs may not represent a contiguous fleet. The rows themselves still support only a low-impact, quickly cleared event interpretation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the export provenance together with the fleet inventory or inverter-ID assignment scheme, so coverage sparsity is not inferred from the maximum ID alone.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific files and fields, including `dispatch_blocks.csv`, `dsm_penalty_rs`, `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `schedule_source`, `tracker_stow_state`, `availability_pct`, and `inverter_events.csv`.
It reproduces the headline calculation explicitly: "(662,444.09 − 453,085.88)/662,444.09 = 31.60%" and distinguishes modelled from settled figures.
It explicitly identifies the missing counterfactual: "Not identified: the counterfactual DSM on 29 May absent the pilot."

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests multiple alternative explanations, including weather, whole-day performance, outage/curtailment, cherry-picked baseline, firmware changes, and schedule-level differences.
It uses the same-day schedule fields to estimate a narrower mechanical comparison: "recomputed 29 May with `base_schedule_mw` → Rs 549,664" and a Rs 96,578 difference from the submitted schedule.

It triangulates day totals, block-level performance, weather fields, availability, curtailment, inverter events, tariff bands, and settlement documentation rather than relying only on the impact note.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It clearly distinguishes arithmetic reproduction from causal inference: "The number is arithmetically real but is n=1 vs n=1" and "Not supported as a causal effect."

It correctly warns that the block bootstrap interval has "fake precision" because treatment is assigned at day level and identifies day-specific severity, schedule level, and forecast luck as unresolved confounders.
It states that the mechanical 17.6% estimate assumes generation would have been identical without the schedule cut and calls that assumption untestable here.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation is proportionate: "Continue as a measurement exercise, not a deployment" rather than either claiming success or abandoning the pilot entirely.
The proposed next test is discriminating: "Within-day block-randomised stow assignment," with settlement against DISCOM data and logged submission timestamps.
The actions preserve operational safeguards through capped revisions, gate verification, reconciliation, and an explicit stopping rule.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion meets the central requirement by separating "pilot day performed better" from the unsupported claim that the pilot caused a 31.6% reduction.

It retains a smaller possible benefit rather than overcorrecting to no value, reporting the same-day mechanical effect as 17.6% and a broader descriptive association while appropriately limiting causal interpretation.
It identifies the omitted conventional days and shows that the headline is sensitive to the comparator: "against 4 Jun it is +12.3% worse."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: the 31.6% arithmetic is reproduced from 28 May and 29 May day totals; this is well supported by the cited `dsm_penalty_rs` calculation.
Observed: additional conventional STOW days and their totals are identified from `dispatch_blocks.csv`; the submission provides a relevant correction to the headline comparator.
Inferred but appropriately qualified: the 17.6% same-day difference is the mechanical effect of replacing the submitted schedule with `base_schedule_mw`; it is not a causal pilot estimate.

Overstated inference: "Weather is not the explanation" is stronger than the cited gust comparisons support. Similar gust maxima and means do not rule out other weather, irradiance, forecast-error, or within-day conditions.
Potentially unsupported inference: "firmware_version 4.7→4.8 ... affecting controls only" establishes a timing difference but does not establish the magnitude or direction of its effect.

Strongest evidence use: the submission directly uses the 29 May `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw` comparison, while preserving the caveat that identical generation is an untestable assumption.

Largest unsupported leap: treating a limited set of gust summaries as sufficient to reject weather-related confounding categorically; this should be narrowed to saying those measured gust metrics do not explain the difference.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot day was descriptively better than the selected 28 May comparator and the schedule revision mechanically reduced modelled DSM, but the evidence supports at most a modest same-day operational benefit—not a causal 31.6% reduction. The true pilot effect could be smaller, larger, or zero because day-level stow severity, forecast conditions, schedule level, and settlement status remain unresolved.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain settled block-level data and complete timestamped gate records, then run the proposed within-day randomized base-versus-pilot comparison while reporting weather and forecast covariates more comprehensively; this would directly test whether the observed mechanical reduction survives settlement and causal assignment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the control finding to “review_note.txt L1,” the filed value to “declaration.pdf p.1,” and the jurisdictional code distinction to “country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Read Me r1.”

It identifies the schema limitations with the exact fields and statements: “one `hts_code`, ‘pad/truncate to eight characters’” and “Not yet modeled: code-system identifier, nomenclature version, effective dates.”
It separately cites “commercial_invoice.pdf” and “air_waybill.pdf” for the valuation discrepancy and explicitly notes that neither document states a tariff code.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission tests and rejects the hypothesis that the “Broker used a wrong/obsolete code” by comparing the Swiss Matrix row for “90211000 from 2025-01-01” with the absence of “90211090.”

It distinguishes the code-system explanation from the vintage explanation: “the Helios value is EU-lineage and mapping-derived, so the gap is code-system, not vintage (vintage is a secondary defect).”
It also avoids treating related documents as corroboration, stating: “Invoice/AWB corroborate 90211090. Rejected: neither states any tariff code.”

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The submission identifies unresolved evidence precisely: “As-of-2025-11-04 master snapshot; Tares entry / ruling for P1001; duty rates for 90211000 vs 90211090; the control's field-mapping spec.”
It qualifies the revenue conclusion as “revenue effect unproven, likely nil” rather than asserting that no duty impact exists.

Confidence levels are stated for individual claims, including lower confidence of “Moderate 70%” for the duty-impact inference, and the conclusion avoids escalation as a declaration error while still raising control and reference-data defects.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains the mechanism as a “cross-code-system comparison,” supported by the Read Me statement that “EU entries use CN8; Switzerland uses a Swiss local tariff code.”
It connects the commercial master to the mismatch by citing that “Migration mappings were used where a local approved code was not supplied.”

It identifies a structural lineage problem in the canonical schema: “Not yet modeled: code-system identifier, nomenclature version, effective dates,” and separately recognizes the post-filing “Master Snapshot Date 2025-12-31” as a versioning defect.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The proposed action is generally proportionate: “Suspend the CH leg of the rule pending re-spec; request the 2025-11-04 master snapshot and the control field map.”

It avoids an unsupported filing action: “Do not amend the filed declaration,” consistent with the evidence that 90211000 is present in the Swiss Matrix and that the alleged mismatch is not itself proof of a declaration error.
The action could be safer with explicit interim monitoring or a bounded review of the invoice discrepancy, and “suspend” is somewhat broad given that the exact control field mapping remains unknown.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Declared 90211000 is the approved Swiss code for P1001” is supported by the cited matrix only to the extent that the matrix is authoritative; the submission does not independently establish the matrix’s approval status or completeness.

“Revenue effect unproven, likely nil” is appropriately qualified but remains an inference: the cited reference files lack duty rates, so zero actual revenue effect cannot be established from the declaration’s 0.0% rate alone.

“The gap is code-system, not vintage” is well supported as the leading explanation, but the missing 2025-11-04 master snapshot and control field map mean a mixed code-system/versioning mechanism cannot be fully ruled out.
The conclusion that there were “3 unlisted reference files extra” is not independently explained beyond the manifest comparison, so the operational significance of those files is unclear.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The control may have been intentionally comparing a commercial or EU CN8 master value with a Swiss declaration code, in which case the declaration is correct but the control’s comparison design or translation layer is incomplete. Alternatively, the Swiss matrix or product mapping could be incomplete; the missing as-of filing-date master snapshot, field-mapping specification, and Tares/ruling evidence prevent conclusively excluding that possibility.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and analyze the 2025-11-04 master snapshot and the control field-mapping specification, explicitly documenting whether the comparison is intended to reconcile Swiss local codes through an effective-dated jurisdictional mapping rather than compare raw strings.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission ties the central findings to precise records, including "declaration.pdf p1 header + line 1," "commercial_invoice.pdf p1," "supplier_origin_register.csv row 9," and "supplier_declaration_reference.txt."
It identifies the relevant values and limitations, including "Packet names no supplier ID, so SUP-01 vs SUP-02 is unresolvable here" and that the register is an "assertion, not proof."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: The submission tests competing explanations in a dedicated section, including "Absence in ClearView proves the claim is unsupported," "The register contradicts the declaration," and "Deliberate misdeclaration."

It appropriately rejects treating the expired SUP-02 record as dispositive because "nothing ties this shipment to SUP-02," but the conclusion that "Consistency plus nil gain indicates a field defect, not evasion" is stronger than the evidence supports.

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: The submission correctly states that "Duty at stake [is] not computable from the packet" and identifies the missing "MFN rate for 90211090" as material.

However, it also asserts "no benefit was obtained" and calls the issue "a data-field defect, not a duty loss" before establishing the MFN rate, while assigning high confidence to conclusions despite stating that the register is not always updated and that supplier linkage is unresolved.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: The submission explains relevant data-lineage issues: "Helios carries manufacturing country. It was never designed to prove preference," and the control "searched only SUP-02."

It distinguishes manufacturing country from preferential origin and identifies the missing linkage between the shipment and supplier records, but it does not fully explain how the declaration's "Preference = Yes" field could represent either a preferential claim or a generic duty-free/MFN indicator beyond identifying that possibility.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: The proposed investigation is generally proportionate and reversible: "obtain from broker BRK-D the filing rationale" and "pull the TARIC MFN rate," while stating "Do not amend IE-2025-000411."

The containment hold on "further preferential entries" is defensible pending clarification, but "renew SD-SUP-02-P1006-2024 regardless" is not supported when the submission also says the shipment's supplier is unresolved and nothing ties it to SUP-02.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No proof of origin exists in the packet" is overbroad because the packet contains a register entry for a valid US declaration, although it does not establish that the declaration belongs to this shipment or provide the underlying document.
"The EU has no FTA with the US, so no agreement can be named" is uncited and does not exclude other legal bases for a zero-duty or preference-related field.
"No benefit was obtained" and "a data-field defect, not a duty loss" are premature because the submission itself says the applicable MFN rate and exposure are not yet computable.
"Consistency plus nil gain indicates a field defect, not evasion" improperly treats consistency and an apparently zero duty payment as sufficient to reject deliberate or other explanations.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may genuinely have US preferential origin supported by the valid SUP-01 declaration, with the supplier linkage omitted from the packet; alternatively, Preference = Yes may be a generic broker or system flag for an erga-omnes duty-free MFN rate. These interpretations cannot be distinguished until the supplier identity, underlying origin declaration, filing rationale and MFN rate are obtained.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Resolve the shipment-to-supplier linkage and verify the TARIC MFN rate and broker coding basis before asserting that origin is unsupported, that no duty loss occurred, or that the issue is merely a data-field defect.

"coa_available_ts and deviation_closed_ts"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that if the 42 open batches close at a median of ≤24 hours, the "21.3h median stands" is not logically guaranteed; adding 42 completed observations could change the overall completed median and does not resolve the SOP evidence-start definition.

The assertion that the 18 INDEX_PENDING CoAs are specifically a CertVault nightly-index artifact is presented with only medium confidence and should remain a hypothesis until portal-versus-index event data is verified.
Refreshing qcore_release_ts for the 42 open batches can test censoring, but it cannot by itself establish that qcore_release_ts is the decision time rather than an interface commit or ETL timestamp.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent long cycle time may be substantially a measurement artifact: QCore release timestamps could represent nightly interface commits rather than disposition decisions, while the extract also combines non-coherent QCore and LabTrack snapshots. A genuine workflow delay remains possible, but the current data cannot separate it from interface timing without event or decision timestamps.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Prioritize a small event-semantics test before relying on the refreshed KPI: obtain QCore's timestamp definition plus a sample event log containing evidence-available, disposition-decision, interface-commit, and release timestamps for the 42 open batches and several 02:10-stamped completed batches. This would distinguish workflow delay from interface timing while also addressing the SOP start event.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Total apparent value, 24 lines: $166,495.60" and the candidate-match table provide line-level request, catalog, basis, value, bucket, and blocker evidence.
"Stock 35 days stale: source_freshness.csv: MaintStar-global 2026-06-26 vs QCore 2026-07-31" explicitly ties the freshness claim to named source fields.
"2 corrupt availability rows: ME-0006, HA-0022 = -1 vs positive on_hand" triangulates availability across spare_parts.csv fields and restrictions.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Descriptions are the problem; semantic search fixes it. Rejected" tests the retrieval hypothesis against blank manufacturer-part-number rates and value concentration.
"Better search cuts spend. Rejected" separates search discovery from policy and reservation constraints.

The analysis identifies several mechanisms—identity quality, revision mismatch, reservation, and stale availability—but does not directly test whether a semantic-search pilot would improve candidate recall after MDM cleanup.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Zero actionable now" is a deliberately conservative operational conclusion tied to the "35 days stale" MaintStar-global source.
"Live-confirm ceiling: $48,592.41, not $166k" usefully distinguishes apparent candidate value from currently supportable value.

Confidence percentages such as "Certain 98%" and "High 92%" are not explained or statistically bounded, and the claim that live confirmation can move the full $48,592.41 to actionable depends on unresolved engineering and reservation checks.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Fund-reduced; MDM cleanup first" reframes the request away from an unqualified savings case.
"1. Live on-hand + reservation extract (<24h)" is a reversible, decision-relevant next step with a quantified potential impact.

The recommendation does not propose a safeguarded semantic-search candidate-generation pilot, so it may prematurely prioritize MDM over testing retrieval value and does not specify success criteria for the cleanup.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects four competing narratives: "Descriptions are the problem," "It's a portfolio opportunity," "Better search cuts spend," and "Only cross-site transfer is at stake."
Each rejection is supported with quantified evidence, including "11 lines / $32,217.96 (19.4%) have stock on the requesting site's own row" and the MTR/VLV concentration figures.
The next-evidence list states what could revive alternatives, including revA/revB interchangeability, reservation release, and interpretation of negative availability.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: The prioritized first request—"Live on-hand + reservation extract (<24h)"—directly tests the largest uncertainty and identifies the potential value it could unlock.
The follow-up requests are discriminating rather than generic: negative-quantity semantics, OEM revision interchangeability, and whether critical reservations can be released with replenishment.
The list also identifies the item-master intervention needed to measure future pilot benefit: "Mandatory-MPN + UoM dictionary in the item master."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "MDM, not embeddings" is too categorical: the evidence supports MDM as a major identity-quality issue, but does not establish that semantic search has no incremental value as candidate generation.

"Zero actionable now" is a defensible conservative posture, but it is stronger than the evidence if local stock or requesting-site availability can be confirmed independently of the stale MaintStar-global snapshot.

"moves up to $48,592.41 (29.2%) into actionable" assumes that live availability confirmation will resolve the remaining engineering, qualification, UOM, and reservation constraints; the extract alone cannot guarantee that outcome.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may still be valuable as a controlled candidate-generation layer even if it cannot establish transferability or savings. MDM cleanup and semantic retrieval are complementary: the former improves identity quality, while the latter can recover candidates from descriptions and blank request MPNs, subject to the same revision, UOM, qualification, reservation, and freshness gates.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a small, reversible retrieval pilot on the 11 blank-MPN requests, comparing normalized exact/structured matching with semantic candidate generation against engineer-validated matches, while using a fresh on-hand/reservation extract. Measure recall, false-positive rate, engineering review time, and confirmed transferable value rather than treating candidate value as savings.
